message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) depending on the exact route you take. On a clear day, with no major stops and staying within speed limits, you can expect the trip to take around **6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic can be heavy, add an extra hour or two. And if you plan to stop for meals, sightseeing, or refueling, factor that in as well.  

So, a typical drive under normal conditions is about **6 hours**; plan for 7–8 hours if you want to be safe and comfortable.

We can provide approximate driving distance (~383 miles via I-5) and typical driving time (~6 hours). But we might also mention traffic, speed limits, etc. The user didn't ask for a tip calculation. So no function call needed. Just answer.
